source_text:
Ἐντέλλομαί σοι, φησίν, φυλάσσειν τὴν ἁγνείαν, καὶ μὴ ἀναβαινέτω σου ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν περὶ γυναικὸς ἀλλοτρίας ἢ περὶ πορνείας τινὸς ἢ περὶ τοιούτων τινῶν ὁμοιωμάτων πονηρῶν. τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν μεγάλην ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζῃ. τῆς δὲ σῆς μνημονεύων πάντοτε γυναικὸς οὐδέποτε διαμαρτήσεις.
ἐὰν γὰρ αὕτη ἡ ἐνθύμησις ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, διαμαρτήσεις, καὶ ἐὰν ἕτερα οὕτως πονηρά, ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζῃ: ἡ γὰρ ἐνθύμησις αὕτη θεοῦ δούλῳ ἁμαρτία μεγάλη ἐστίν: ἐὰν δέ τις ἐργάσηται τὸ ἔργον τὸ πονηρὸν τοῦτο, θάνατον ἑαυτῷ κατεργάζεται.
βλέπε οὖν σύ: ἀπέχου ἀπὸ τῆς ἐνθυμήσεως ταύτης: ὅπου γὰρ σεμνότης κατοικεῖ, ἐκεῖ ἀνομία οὐκ ὀφείλει ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνδρὸς δικαίου.
λέγω αὐτῷ: Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ὀλίγα ἐπερωτῆσαί σε. Λέγε, φησίν. Κύριε, φημί, εἰ γυναῖκα ἔχῃ τις πιστὴν ἐν κυρίῳ καὶ ταύτην εὕρῃ ἐν μοιχείᾳ τινί, ἆρα ἁμαρτάνει ὁ ἀνὴρ συνζῶν μετ’ αὐτῆς;
Ἄχρι τῆς ἀγνοίας, φησίν, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει: ἐὰν δὲ γνῷ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν αὐτῆς καὶ μὴ μετανοήσῃ ἡ γυνή, ἀλλ’ ἐπιμένῃ τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς καὶ συνζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ μετ’ αὐτῆς, ἔνοχος γίνεται τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῆς καὶ κοινωνὸς τῆς μοιχείας αὐτῆς.
Τί οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ποιήσῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐὰν ἐπιμείνῃ τῷ πάθει τούτῳ ἡ γυνή; Ἀπολυσάτω, φησίν, αὐτὴν καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἐφ̓ ἑαυτῷ μενέτω: ἐὰν δὲ ἀπολύσας τὴν γυναῖκα ἑτέραν γαμήσῃ, καὶ αὐτὸς μοιχᾶται.
Ἐὰν οὖν, φημί, κύριε, μετὰ τὸ ἀπολυθῆναι τὴν γυναῖκα μετανοήσῃ ἡ γυνὴ καὶ θελήσῃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἑαυτῆς ἄνδρα ὑποστρέψαι, οὐ παραδεχθήσεται;
Καὶ μήν, φησίν, ἐὰν μὴ παραδέξηται αὐτὴν ὁ ἀνήρ, ἁμαρτάνει καὶ μεγάλην ἁμαρτίαν ἑαυτῷ ἐπισπᾶται, ἀλλὰ δεῖ παραδεχθῆναι τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα καὶ μετανοοῦντα, μὴ ἐπὶ πολὺ δέ: τοῖς γὰρ δούλοις τοῦ θεοῦ μετάνοιά ἐστιν μία. διὰ τὴν μετάνοιαν οὖν οὐκ ὀφείλει γαμεῖν ὁ ἀνήρ. αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις ἐπὶ γυναικὶ καὶ ἀνδρὶ κεῖται.
οὐ μόνον, φησίν, μοιχεία ἐστίν, ἐάν τις τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ μιάνῃ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὃς ἂν τὰ ὁμοιώματα ποιῇ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, μοιχᾶται. ὥστε καὶ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις ἔργοις ἐὰν ἐμμένῃ τις καὶ μὴ μετανοῇ, ἀπέχου ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ συνζῆθι αὐτῷ: εἰ δὲ μή, καὶ σὺ μέτοχος εἶ τῆς ἀμαρτίας αὐτοῦ.
διὰ τοῦτο προσετάγη ὑμῖν ἐφ̓ ἑαυτοῖς μένειν, εἴτε ἀνὴρ εἴτε γυνή: δύναται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις μετάνοια εἶναι.
ἐγὼ οὖν, φησίν, οὐ δίδωμι ἀφορμήν, ἵνα αὕτη ἡ πρᾶξις οὕτως συντελῆται, ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ μηκέτι ἁμαρτάνειν τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα. περὶ δὲ τῆς προτέρας ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ὁ δυνάμενος ἴασιν δοῦναι: αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἔχων πάντων τὴν ἐξουσίαν.
Ἠρώτησα δὲ αὐτὸν πάλιν λέγων: Ἐπεὶ ὁ κύριος ἄξιόν με ἡγήσατο, ἵνα μετ’ ἐμοῦ πάντοτε κατοικῇς, ὀλίγα μου ῥήματα ἔτι ἀνάσχου, ἐπεὶ οὐ συνίω οὐδὲν καὶ ἡ καρδία μου πεπώρωται ἀπὸ τῶν προτέρων μου πράξεων: συνέτισόν με, ὅτι λίαν ἄφρων εἰμὶ καὶ ὅλως οὐθὲν νοῶ.
ἀποκριθείς μοι λέγει: Ἐγώ, φησίν, ἐπὶ τῆς μετανοίας εἰμὶ καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς μετανοοῦσιν σύνεσιν δίδωμι. ἢ οὐ δοκεῖ σοι, φησίν, αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ μετανοῆσαι σύνεσιν εἶναι; τὸ μετανοῆσαι, φησίν, σύνεσίς ἐστιν μεγάλη: συνίει γὰρ ὁ ἁμαρτήσας, ὅτι πεποίηκεν τὸ πονηρὸν ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ἀναβαίνει ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ἡ πρᾶξις, ἣν ἔπραξεν, καὶ μετανοεῖ καὶ οὐκέτι ἐργάζεται τὸ πονηρόν, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἀγαθὸν πολυτελῶς ἐργάζεται καὶ ταπεινοῖ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν καὶ βασανίζει, ὅτι ἥμαρτεν. βλέπεις οὖν, ὅτι ἡ μετάνοια σύνεσίς ἐστιν μεγάλη.
Διὰ τοῦτο οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἐξακριβάζομαι παρὰ σοῦ πάντα: πρῶτον μέν, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, ἵνα γνῶ, ποῖα ἔργα ἐργαζόμενος ζήσομαι, ὅτι πολλαί μου εἰσὶν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι καὶ ποικίλαι.
Ζήσῃ, φησίν, ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολάς μου φυλάξῃς καὶ πορευθῇς ἐν αὐταῖς: καὶ ὃς ἂν ἀκούσας τὰς ἐντολὰς ταύτας φυλάξῃ, ζήσεται τῷ θεῷ.
Ἔτι, φημί, κύριε, προσθήσω τοῦ ἐπερωτῆσαι. Λέγε, φησίν. Ἤκουσα, φημί, κύριε, παρά τινων διδασκάλων, ὅτι ἑτέρα μετάνοια οὐκ ἔστιν εἰ μὴ ἐκείνη, ὅτε εἰς ὕδωρ κατέβημεν καὶ ἐλάβομεν ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν τῶν προτέρων.
λέγει μοι: Καλῶς ἤκουσας: οὕτω γὰρ ἔχει. ἔδει γὰρ τὸν εἰληφότα ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν μηκέτι ἁμαρτάνειν, ἀλλ’ ἐν ἁγνείᾳ κατοικεῖν.
ἐπεὶ δὲ πάντα ἐξακριβάζῃ, καὶ τοῦτό σοι δηλώσω, μὴ διδοὺς ἀφορμὴν τοῖς μέλλουσι πιστεύειν ἢ τοῖς νῦν πιστεύσασιν εἰς τὸν κύριον. οἱ γὰρ νῦν πιστεύσαντες ἢ μέλλοντες πιστεύειν μετάνοιαν ἁμαρτιῶν οὐκ ἔχουσιν, ἄφεσιν δὲ ἔχουσι τῶν προτέρων ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν.
τοῖς οὖν κληθεῖσι πρὸ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἔθηκεν ὁ κύριος μετάνοιαν: καρδιογνώστης γὰρ ὢν ὁ κύριος καὶ πάντα προγινώσκων ἔγνω τὴν ἀσθένειαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ τὴν πολυπλοκίαν τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι ποιήσει τι κακὸν τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πονηρεύσεται εἰς αὐτούς.
πολύσπλαγχνος οὖν ὢν ὁ κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπὶ τὴν ποίησιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔθηκεν τὴν μετάνοιαν ταύτην, καὶ ἐμοὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τῆς μετανοίας ταύτης ἐδόθη.
ἀλλὰ ἐγώ σοι λέγω, φησί μετὰ τὴν κλῆσιν ἐκείνην τὴν μεγάλην καὶ σεμνὴν ἐάν τις ἐκπειρασθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου ἁμαρτήσῃ, μίαν μετάνοιαν ἔχει: ἐὰν δὲ ὑπὸ χεῖρα ἁμαρτάνῃ καὶ μετανοήσῃ, ἀσύμφορόν ἐστι τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ τοιούτῳ: δυσκόλως γὰρ ζήσεται.
λέγω αὐτῷ Ἐζωοποιήθην ταῦτα παρὰ σοῦ ἀκούσας οὕτως ἀκριβῶς: οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι, ἐὰν μηκέτι προσθήσω ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις μου, σωθήσομαι. Σωθήσῃ, φησίν, καὶ πάντες, ὅσοι ἐὰν ταῦτα ποιήσωσιν.
Ἠρώτησα αὐτὸν πάλιν λέγων: Κύριε, ἐπεὶ ἅπαξ ἀνέχῃ μου, ἔτι μοι καὶ τοῦτο δήλωσον. Λέγε, φησίν. Ἐὰν γυνή, φημί, κύριε, ἢ πάλιν ἀνήρ τις κοιμηθῇ καὶ γαμήσῃ τις ἐξ αὐτῶν, μήτι ἁμαρτάνει ὁ γαμῶν;
Οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει, φησίν: ἐὰν δὲ ἐφ̓ ἑαυτῷ μείνῃ τις, περισσοτέραν ἑαυτῷ τιμὴν καὶ μεγάλην δόξαν περιποιεῖται πρὸς τὸν κύριον: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ γαμήσῃ, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει.
τήρει οὖν τὴν ἁγνείαν καὶ τὴν σεμνότητα, καὶ ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ. ταῦτά σοι ὅσα λαλῶ καὶ μέλλω λαλεῖν, φύλασσε ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν, ἀφ̓ ἧς μοι παρεδόθης ἡμέρας, καὶ εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου κατοικήσω.
τοῖς δὲ προτέροις σου παραπτώμασιν ἄφεσις ἔσται, ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολάς μου φυλάξῃς: καὶ πᾶσι δὲ ἄφεσις ἔσται, ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολάς μου ταύτας φυλάξωσι καὶ πορευθῶσιν ἐν τῇ ἁγνότητι ταύτῃ.
thought_title: The Commandment of Purity and the One Repentance
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the fourth commandment, on purity. Hermas asks about a wife who is unfaithful, about whether there is repentance after baptism, and about marrying again after a husband or wife has died.
pass_a_gloss:
I command you, he says, to guard purity, and let it not go up upon your heart concerning another man's wife or concerning some fornication or concerning some such evil likenesses. For doing this you work a great sin. But remembering always your own wife you will never sin. For if this thought goes up upon your heart, you will sin, and if other things thus evil, you work sin: for this thought is a great sin for a servant of God: but if someone works this evil deed, he works death for himself. See therefore you: keep away from this thought: for where reverence dwells, there lawlessness ought not to go up upon the heart of a righteous man. I say to him: Lord, permit me to ask you a few things. Speak, he says. Lord, I say, if someone has a wife faithful in the Lord and finds her in some adultery, does the husband sin living together with her? Until ignorance, he says, he does not sin: but if the husband knows her sin and the wife does not repent, but remains in her fornication and the husband lives together with her, he becomes guilty of her sin and a sharer of her adultery. What then, I say, lord, should the husband do, if the wife remains in this passion? Let him divorce her, he says, and let the husband remain by himself: but if having divorced the wife he marries another, he also commits adultery. If then, I say, lord, after the wife is divorced the wife repents and wishes to return to her own husband, will she not be received back? And indeed, he says, if the husband does not receive her back, he sins and draws a great sin upon himself, but it is necessary that the one who has sinned and repents be received back, not for long however: for for the servants of God repentance is one. Because of the repentance therefore the husband ought not to marry. This practice lies upon wife and husband. Not only, he says, is it adultery, if someone defiles his flesh, but also whoever does the likenesses of the nations commits adultery. So that also in such works if someone remains and does not repent, keep away from him and do not live together with him: otherwise, you also are a sharer of his sin. Because of this it was commanded to you to remain by yourselves, whether husband or wife: for in such cases repentance can be. I therefore, he says, do not give occasion, that this practice be thus completed, but for the one who has sinned to sin no longer. But concerning his former sin there is the one who is able to give healing: for he himself is the one having authority over all things. I asked him again saying: Since the lord considered me worthy, that you dwell with me always, bear with a few words of mine still, since I understand nothing and my heart has been hardened from my former deeds: make me understand, because I am very foolish and I understand nothing at all. Answering me he says: I, he says, am over repentance and to all who repent I give understanding. Or does it not seem to you, he says, that this very repenting is understanding? Repenting, he says, is great understanding: for the one who has sinned understands that he has done the evil before the lord, and the deed which he did goes up upon his heart, and he repents and no longer works the evil, but works the good abundantly and humbles his own soul and torments it, because he sinned. You see therefore, that repentance is great understanding. Because of this therefore, I say, lord, I inquire precisely from you all things: first, that I am a sinner, that I may know, what works working I will live, because my sins are many and various. You will live, he says, if you guard my commandments and walk in them: and whoever having heard these commandments guards them, will live to God. Still, I say, lord, I will add to ask. Speak, he says. I heard, I say, lord, from some teachers, that there is no other repentance except that one, when we went down into water and received forgiveness of our former sins. He says to me: You heard well: for so it is. For it was necessary that the one who has received forgiveness of sins no longer sin, but dwell in purity. But since you inquire precisely into all things, I will also reveal this to you, not giving occasion to those about to believe or to those now believing in the lord. For those now believing or about to believe do not have repentance of sins, but they have forgiveness of their former sins. For those called before these days the lord established repentance: for the lord being knower of hearts and foreknowing all things knew the weakness of humans and the many-twistedness of the devil, that he will do some evil to the servants of God and will act wickedly toward them. Being therefore very compassionate the lord had compassion on his creation and established this repentance, and to me the authority of this repentance was given. But I say to you, he says, after that great and reverent calling if someone tempted by the devil sins, he has one repentance: but if he sins repeatedly and repents, it is unprofitable for such a man: for with difficulty he will live. I say to him: I have been made alive hearing these things from you so precisely: for I know that, if I no longer add to my sins, I will be saved. You will be saved, he says, and all, as many as do these things. I asked him again saying: Lord, since once you bear with me, reveal also this to me. Speak, he says. If a wife, I say, lord, or again some husband falls asleep and someone of them marries, does the one marrying sin? He does not sin, he says: but if someone remains by himself, he acquires for himself more abundant honor and great glory before the lord: but if he also marries, he does not sin. Guard therefore purity and reverence, and you will live to God. These things, as many as I speak and am about to speak, guard from now, from the day on which you were handed over to me, and I will dwell in your house.
But for your former transgressions there will be forgiveness, if you keep my commandments; and for all also there will be forgiveness, if they keep these my commandments and walk in this purity.

choices.why: The commandment concerns sexual purity in thought and deed; 'purity' keeps the moral force without narrowing to 'chastity' or 'cleanliness'.
The term denotes an inner impulse or reflection that rises upon the heart; 'thought' preserves the inward, pre-action character.
The phrase refers to acts resembling the sins of the nations; 'likenesses' keeps the comparative sense of the Greek.
The imperative is a command to the husband; 'divorce' is the plain legal sense in this marital context.
The compound is a title of God; the literal rendering preserves the theological weight.
The noun describes the devil's intricate scheming; the literal compound keeps the image of many folds or twists.
The term denotes specific acts of falling away or missteps, distinct from a general state of sin; 'transgressions' preserves the concrete, countable sense.
The standard rendering for release from guilt; the glossary does not cover this term, but 'forgiveness' is the plain sense in context of past wrongs.
The Shepherd's instructions are consistently called commandments; this keeps the legal-teaching register of the work.
The verb denotes a way of life, not mere movement; 'walk' preserves the biblical idiom of conduct.
The Shepherd has just commanded purity (ἁγνεία) and reverence; 'purity' keeps the connection to the preceding instruction.

pass_b_english: “I command you,” the Shepherd said, “to guard purity. Let no thought rise in your heart about another man’s wife, or about any sexual immorality, or about any evil things of that kind. For if you do this, you commit a great sin. But if you always keep your own wife in mind, you will never go wrong.

“For if this thought rises in your heart, you will go wrong. And if other things just as evil rise in it, you commit sin. For to a servant of God this thought is a great sin. And if anyone carries out this evil deed, he brings death upon himself.
“So watch yourself. Keep away from this thought. For where reverence dwells, lawlessness ought not to rise in the heart of a righteous man.”

I said to him, “Sir, allow me to ask you a few things.” “Speak,” he said. “Sir,” I said, “if a man has a wife who believes in the Lord, and he finds her in some act of adultery, does the husband sin if he goes on living with her?”

“As long as he does not know,” the Shepherd said, “he does not sin. But suppose the husband comes to know of her sin, and the wife does not repent but persists in her immorality. If the husband then goes on living with her, he becomes guilty of her sin and a partner in her adultery.”

“What then, sir,” I said, “is the husband to do, if the wife persists in this passion?” “Let him divorce her,” he said, “and let the husband remain by himself. But if he divorces his wife and marries another, he too commits adultery.”
“If then, sir,” I said, “after the wife has been divorced, she repents and wants to return to her own husband, will she not be taken back?”

“Yes indeed,” he said. “If the husband does not take her back, he sins and brings a great sin upon himself. The one who has sinned and repents must be taken back, but not many times. For the servants of God have one repentance. So, for the sake of repentance, the husband ought not to marry. This rule holds for wife and husband alike.

“Adultery,” he said, “is not only when someone defiles his flesh. Whoever does the kind of things the nations do also commits adultery. So if anyone persists in such deeds and does not repent, keep away from him and do not live with him. Otherwise you too have a share in his sin.
“This is why you were commanded to remain by yourselves, whether husband or wife. For in such cases there can be repentance.

“So I am not giving an excuse,” he said, “for this thing to be done. I speak so that the one who has sinned may sin no more. As for his former sin, there is one who is able to give healing, for he is the one who has authority over all things.”

I asked him again, “Since the Lord has counted me worthy to have you dwell with me always, bear with a few more words from me. For I understand nothing, and my heart has been hardened by my former deeds. Give me understanding, for I am very foolish and grasp nothing at all.”

He answered me, “I am set over repentance, and I give understanding to all who repent. Or do you not think,” he said, “that to repent is itself understanding? To repent,” he said, “is great understanding. For the one who has sinned understands that he has done evil before the Lord. The deed he did rises in his heart, and he repents and no longer does evil. Instead he does good lavishly, and he humbles his own soul and torments it, because he sinned. You see, then, that repentance is great understanding.”
“That is why, sir,” I said, “I question you so exactly about everything. First, because I am a sinner, I ask so that I may know what works I must do to live. For my sins are many and of many kinds.”
“You will live,” he said, “if you keep my commandments and walk in them. And whoever hears these commandments and keeps them will live to God.”

“Sir,” I said, “I will ask one thing more.” “Speak,” he said. “Sir,” I said, “I have heard from certain teachers that there is no other repentance except the one when we went down into the water and received forgiveness of our former sins.”
He said to me, “You have heard rightly, for so it is. The one who has received forgiveness of sins ought to sin no more, but to live in purity.

“But since you ask about everything so exactly, I will make this clear to you as well. I do not say it to give an excuse to those who are going to believe, or to those who have now come to believe in the Lord. For those who have now believed, or are going to believe, have no repentance for sins. What they have is forgiveness of their former sins.

“So it was for those who were called before these days that the Lord appointed repentance. For the Lord knows the heart, and he knows all things before they happen. He knew the weakness of human beings and the great cunning of the devil. He knew that the devil would do some evil to the servants of God and deal wickedly with them.
“So the Lord, who is full of compassion, had compassion on what he had made and appointed this repentance. And the authority over this repentance was given to me.

“But I tell you,” he said, “after that great and solemn calling, if anyone is tempted by the devil and sins, he has one repentance. But if he sins again and again and repents, it is of no use to such a person, for he will live only with difficulty.”

I said to him, “I was brought to life when I heard these things from you so exactly. For I know that if I add no more to my sins, I will be saved.” “You will be saved,” he said, “and so will all who do these things.”

I asked him again, “Sir, since you bear with me this once, make this clear to me as well.” “Speak,” he said. “Sir,” I said, “if a wife, or again a husband, falls asleep in death, and one of them marries, does the one who marries sin?”
“He does not sin,” the Shepherd said. “But if he remains by himself, he gains greater honor for himself and great glory with the Lord. Yet even if he marries, he does not sin.

“So guard purity and reverence, and you will live to God. Everything I am telling you, and everything I am going to tell you, keep from now on, from the day you were handed over to me, and I will dwell in your house.
“For your former transgressions there will be forgiveness, if you keep my commandments. And there will be forgiveness for all, if they keep these commandments of mine and walk in this purity.”

problems.quote: if he sins repeatedly and repents
problems.source_quote: ἐὰν δὲ ὑπὸ χεῖρα ἁμαρτάνῃ καὶ μετανοήσῃ
problems.why: 'ὑπὸ χεῖρα' means 'underhand' or 'secretly', not 'repeatedly'. The distinction is between public temptation and secret sin.
problems.fix: But if he sins underhand and repents
problems.ruling: ὑπὸ χεῖρα means 'secretly/underhand,' not 'repeatedly'; mistranslates the key distinction.

edits.old: But if he sins repeatedly and repents, it is of no benefit to such a person.
edits.new: But if he sins underhand and repents, it is of no benefit to such a person.

problems.quote: I, then," he says, "am not giving an occasion
problems.why: Complex dialogue with multiple speakers and unclear 'he' references

problems.quote: if anyone carries out this evil deed, he brings death upon himself
problems.why: Adultery 'brings death' but later divorce and remarriage also adultery; inconsistency in severity
problems.fix: Clarify: spiritual death vs. no second repentance

problems.quote: the shepherd, the angel of repentance
problems.why: The same figure is called 'the shepherd,' 'the angel of repentance,' and 'the Shepherd' with inconsistent capitalization.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'the Shepherd (the angel of repentance)'.

problems.quote: But if he sins underhand and repents, it is of no benefit to such a person.
problems.why: 'Underhand' is unclear; likely means 'secretly' or 'deliberately with intent to repent afterward'.
problems.fix: Use 'if he sins deliberately, planning to repent afterward'.

problems.why: Modern English 'underhand' means 'sneaky'; the context needs 'deliberately' or 'with premeditation'.
problems.fix: Use 'if he sins deliberately, planning to repent later'.

edits.old: But if he sins underhand and repents, it is of no benefit to such a person.
edits.new: But if he sins deliberately, planning to repent afterward, it is of no benefit to such a person.

fixed: Speaker transitions: The source uses 'φησίν' and 'λέγει μοι' consistently; the English already marks the Shepherd's speech with 'he says' and Hermas's with 'I say'. No change needed.

Adultery severity: The source says 'θάνατον ἑαυτῷ κατεργάζεται' (works death for himself), which the English renders as 'brings death upon himself'. This is accurate; the later discussion of divorce and remarriage is a separate case. No change needed.
Shepherd capitalization: The work brief's cast lists 'The Shepherd' as the angel of repentance, and the English consistently uses 'the Shepherd' or 'he' in context. No change needed.
